content: Avoid coadministration of elvitegravir with CYP3A inducers, as this may lead to reduced plasma concentrations of elvitegravir and/or any concomitantly administered protease inhibitors. This reduction can result in a loss of therapeutic efficacy and potentially lead to drug resistance. Close monitoring is recommended. Quinidine increases elvitegravir levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Elvitegravir, being a CYP3A4 substrate, may have increased levels when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Close monitoring is advised. Elvitegravir can increase the levels or effects of quizartinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. If quizartinib is coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, its dose should be reduced to 4 mg/day. If the dose is 7 mg/day, quizartinib should be interrupted during the use of strong CYP3A inhibitors. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for five half-lives, resume the previous quizartinib dose. Ribociclib increases elvitegravir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and is contraindicated. Rifabutin decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternative drugs or modify therapy and monitor closely. Rifampin also decreases elvitegravir levels via CYP3A4 induction and should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Rifapentine reduces elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Ritonavir increases elvitegravir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rucaparib also increases elvitegravir levels through CYP3A4 inhibition, requiring therapy modification and close monitoring. St. John’s Wort decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Stiripentol, a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, can alter the effects of coadministered CYP3A4 substrates. Monitor closely and adjust dosages as needed. Tazemetostat decreases elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Tecovirimat, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, may reduce elvitegravir levels. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if coadministered. Tipranavir’s effect on elvitegravir levels is unknown, but the recommended dose is 150 mg of elvitegravir once daily with tipranavir/ritonavir 500/200 mg twice daily. Use caution and monitor closely. Tucatinib increases elvitegravir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of the CYP3A substrate according to product labeling and monitor closely. Ublituximab may decrease elvitegravir’s effects due to immunosuppressive properties, increasing the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Voclosporin and elvitegravir coadministration may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Drugs associated with nephrotoxicity may heighten the risk of acute or chronic kidney damage. Voriconazole increases elvitegravir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Elvitegravir may decrease warfarin levels or effects by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Zinc reduces elvitegravir levels by binding to it in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer elvitegravir two hours before or six hours after zinc-containing products. Elvitegravir is an integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI) that blocks the integration of HIV-1 DNA into the host genome, preventing the formation of the HIV-1 provirus and halting viral replication. This mechanism is essential for managing HIV-1 infections. For formulary information, create a list of plans to compare drug statuses within the same class. This list can be saved and edited as needed. Contact the applicable plan provider for the most current information, as formulary details may vary and change over time.
